items.author: OldmanScalping
items.context: Oldman Crypto (en inglés), tres semanas después del hackeo de Binance por $6.400M: solo se recuperaron $32M, $2.820M están congelados y $2.670M siguen en manos de los atacantes (según SomaXBT), que movieron ~$594M en ETH vía THORChain el 19 y 20-nov. Los 18.270 BTC robados no se han movido. Binance cubrió las pérdidas con reservas propias ($6.340M+). Termina con una pregunta abierta. Post de ~5 min con 0 respuestas.
items.suggested_text:
The number that stands out to me is the 18,270 BTC that hasn't moved. Stolen ETH can be pushed through THORChain in days, but a BTC pile that size is watched by every chain-analysis desk, so moving it means choosing between speed and getting flagged. Sitting still is also a strategy.

The other lesson is on the customer side. Users were made whole only because Binance had $6.34B+ in reserves to absorb the hit. That's a solvency decision by one company, not a property of keeping coins on an exchange. A platform without that cushion would be having a very different conversation with its users.

Recovery figures measure how good the investigators are. Whether your coins were ever part of the loss was decided long before the hack.
